lifecycle_gaps_retained: Whether any act taken under the Section V exemption power before 1945-08-21 left surviving effects is not examined.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held working text of the order, both history observations (a 2026-10-15 Federal Register API disposition note and a 1989 printed codification row), and the acting text. The two observations are editorial leads and are not the basis; the basis is the acting instrument's own held text. EO 9248 (signed 1942-09-17, 7 FR 7419) has one operative paragraph that restates Section V of Executive Order No. 9240 of September 9, 1942 (Regulations Relating to Overtime Wage Compensation) so that the Secretary of Labor may exempt industries or occupations. It has no independent life apart from EO 9240. Executive Order 9601 (signed 1945-08-21, 10 FR 10275) orders that EO 9240, as amended, entitled Regulations Relating to Overtime Wage Compensation, is revoked, effective as of the date of that order, with no partial qualifier or savings clause in the held text. Because the revocation reaches 9240 as amended, it extinguishes the Section V text supplied by 9248, so the single clause ended 1945-08-21. Partial scope and savings checked: none found in the held texts. The 1989 snapshot agrees but is not the basis.
